title: RMFlow: Refined Mean Flow by a Noise-Injection Step for Multimodal Generation
claim: On a toy multimodal density, a one-step baseline misses peaks and valleys, while adding a refinement step matches the data as well as many-step sampling.
layout: 2x2 grid of density plots with a shared legend box on top, captions under each plot, and the right and bottom edges cut off
description: A shared legend box at the top shows a solid blue line labeled Sample and a dashed orange line labeled Data. Below it is a grid of 1-D density plots, with p(x) on the y-axis (0 to 0.8) and x on the x-axis (about -2.5 to 2.5). Each plot overlays the sampled density in blue on the true three-peak mixture-Gaussian density in orange dashes. The top-left plot, captioned 1-NFE MeanFlow, shows visible mismatch: the peaks are too low or too high, and the valley near x=1 is filled in. The plot beside it, captioned 8-NFE MeanFlow, fits much more closely. The bottom row's plots fit very tightly, and their captions and any further panels appear to be cropped away. The eye goes first to the legend, then to the blue-versus-orange gaps in the top-left plot.
caption: Contrasting MeanFlow with RMFlow for mixture Gaussian sampling; see Section [ref] for experimental details and more results.
abstract: Mean flow (MeanFlow) enables efficient, high-fidelity image generation, yet its single-function evaluation (1-NFE) generation often cannot yield compelling results. We address this issue by introducing RMFlow, an efficient multimodal generative model that integrates a coarse 1-NFE MeanFlow transport with a subsequent tailored noise-injection refinement step. RMFlow approximates the average velocity of the flow path using a neural network trained with a new loss function that balances minimizing the Wasserstein distance between probability paths and maximizing sample likelihood. RMFlow achieves near state-of-the-art results on text-to-image, context-to-molecule, and time-series generation using only 1-NFE, at a computational cost comparable to the baseline MeanFlows.
